items.text: This I want to believe implicitly: Man was born for love and revolution.
items.author: Osamu Dazai

items.text: If you don't stand for something, you will fall for anything.
items.author: Malcolm X

items.text: There are too many things we do not wish to know about ourselves. People are not, for example, terribly anxious to be equal (equal, after all, to what and to whom?) but they love the idea of being superior.
items.author: James Baldwin

items.text: I’ve had enough of someone else’s propaganda… I’m for truth, no matter who tells it. I’m for justice, no matter who it is for or against. I’m a human being first and foremost, and as such I’m for whoever and whatever benefits humanity as a whole.
items.author: Malcolm X

items.text: If you're not careful, the newspapers will have you hating the people who are being oppressed, and loving the people who are doing the oppressing.

items.text: It is a dangerous thing to unbelieve something only because it frightens you.
items.author: Marissa Meyer

items.text: I could see from this, that perhaps if white Americans could accept the Oneness of God, then perhaps, too, they could accept in reality the Oneness of Man—and cease to measure, and hinder, and harm others in terms of their ‘differences’ in color.
items.author: Malcolm X

items.text:
Fairness is for happy people, for people who have been lucky enough to have lived a life defined more by certainties than by ambiguities.
Right and wrong, however, are for—well, not unhappy people, maybe, but scarred people; scared people.
items.author: Hanya Yanagihara

items.text: Hope is the only thing stronger than fear.
items.author: Suzanne Collins

items.text: But as long as we in the West place on color the value that we do, we make it impossible for the great unwashed to consolidate themselves according to any other principle. Color is not a human or a personal reality; it is a political reality.
items.author: James Baldwin

items.text: One day, may we all meet together in the light of understanding.
items.author: Malcolm X

items.text: But hoping," he said, "is how the impossible can be possible after all.

items.text: There is a luxury in self-reproach. When we blame ourselves, we feel that no one else has a right to blame us. It is the confession, not the priest, that gives us absolution.
